answer: Each identity must lock bonded collateral; evidence of shared control lets the protocol aggregate equivocation rather than treat signers as independent. For k coordinated identities, the penalty scales as O(k²), making a swarm costlier than its nominal headcount suggests. Across repeated detections, asymmetric depreciation compounds capital loss exponentially. A mirror of correlated signing patterns can expose a lotus-like cluster perched on the ledge of a common escrow trail.
